summary: A target-level completion of finite native-root geometry that imports the current Scheme and stack foundations root-stack, quotient and QCoh plans. Eleven residual comparisons/applications specify effective native descent, the upstream universal root, coherent base change, both affine presentations, algebraicity, relative coarse spaces, full fibres, arbitrary-index regularity and the exact DM locus. The canonical root definition and the parent Hopf-coaction invariant calculation remain their accepted owners. One precise finite-diagonalizable coarse-quotient supplier request and the exhaustive baseline-signature boundary remain explicit.

nodes.title: Effective descent of the native root data
nodes.statement: For a scheme T, a native pair (L,s), an integer n≥1 and any fpqc cover U={T_i→T}, the canonical functor D_U:Root_n(T;L,s)→Desc_U(Root_n(L,s)) is an equivalence of groupoids. Its underlying module comparison is the restriction of the imported equivalence QCoh(T)≃Desc_U(QCoh), not a descent functor on chosen frames. The equivalence descends the root line, its section, its power identification and every root arrow, with the native tensor and pullback comparisons. It is compatible, up to specified natural isomorphisms, with refinement of covers and arbitrary base change of T.
hypotheses: Schemes and covers lie in one fixed universe-bounded site; category values may lie in a larger universe.
No Noetherian, separation, finiteness or flatness hypothesis on a subsequent base-change map.
proofSteps: Use SF.1/qcoh-fpqc-descent on all quasi-coherent modules and all linear maps. Descend M_i and the transition isomorphisms; finite-locally-free-descent, including rank, makes the result a native invertible sheaf.

Through the imported strong symmetric monoidal pullback, identify the descended tensor power with M^n and the descended unit with O_T. Descend t_i as maps O→M and descend φ_i:M_i^n→L_i and φ_i inverse. Faithfulness checks that these maps are inverse and that φ(t^n)=s.
Fullness descends each compatible root arrow and its inverse; faithfulness detects its two defining squares, equality and the cocycle. This proves full faithfulness as well as essential surjectivity.

Compare two effective descents by the unique isomorphism inducing their local comparison. The same uniqueness proves refinement, base-change, identity and composition coherence; no chosen global frame enters.
acceptance: Every descent object is recovered with its section and power identification.
D_U induces a bijection on every Hom set, including the automorphisms of a zero-section root.

sources.locator: Proposition 35.5.2 (023T) and Lemma 35.7.6 (05B2); tag pages, no fixed pagination
sources.match: Effective descent includes noninvertible module morphisms; finite locally free rank is fpqc local. Restricting these statements and the tensor comparison yields this root-specific equivalence.

api.name: FiniteRoot.descentEquiv
api.statement: The functor D_U is an equivalence; its unit and counit are root isomorphisms with the native underlying module descent unit and counit.

api.name: FiniteRoot.descentEquiv_section
api.statement: The counit identifies the restriction of the descended t:O_T→M with t_i, through the unit and line-pullback comparisons.

api.name: FiniteRoot.descentEquiv_powerIso
api.statement: After the tensor-power pullback comparison, the counit carries the restricted descended φ and its inverse to φ_i and φ_i inverse.

api.name: FiniteRoot.descentEquiv_hom
api.statement: Compatible local isomorphisms descend uniquely to an isomorphism carrying t to t′ and satisfying φ′∘a^n=φ; neither condition is omitted.

api.name: FiniteRoot.descentEquiv_refine
api.statement: For a refinement V→U, the two effective-descent equivalences are compared by their unique root isomorphism inducing the refinement counit; identity and composite refinements satisfy the triangle and pentagon.

api.name: FiniteRoot.descentEquiv_baseChange
api.statement: Pulling the descent datum to Y→T and then descending is naturally isomorphic to pulling the descended root to Y; the comparison preserves t,φ and has the native pullback identity/composition laws.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.descent_identity
tests.statement: For the singleton identity cover, D_U is equivalent to the identity root functor with its native pullback-unit isomorphism.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.descent_zero_automorphism
tests.statement: For n=2 over Q and the zero root section, the arrows with unit labels 1 and −1 remain distinct after descent along any fpqc cover; replacing the fibres by isomorphism classes fails this test.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.descent_nontrivial_line
tests.statement: For the Zariski cover of P¹_Q by its two standard affines, descend local frames of M=O(1), t=0, φ:M^2≅L=O(2). The descended root line is O(1), which has no global frame.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.descent_nonflat_change
tests.statement: For the root (O,t=2,φ=identity) of (O,4) over Z and n=2, base change to F₂ descends to the zero-section root. The comparison does not cancel t or require Z→F₂ flat.

uses.how: Makes the native root pseudofunctor an fpqc stack before identifying it with a geometric quotient.
Supplies effective finite-level descent without imposing a global frame.

nodes.title: Comparison with the upstream root stack
nodes.statement: For an algebraic stack X with an invertible sheaf L and section s, and n≥1, compare the accepted native root stack R_n(X;L,s) with the already owned upstream rootStack n (L,s)=X×_{[A¹/G_m],θ_n}[A¹/G_m]. There is a strong equivalence E over X. At T, it sends (x,M,t,φ) to the 2-pullback object (x,(M,t),φ), using the native line-section comparison; it sends (a:x→x′,b:M≅M′) to the corresponding pair of arrows with the same compatibility square. For a stack base, the square uses a to identify x*L with x′*L. The quasi-inverse retains the actual isomorphism φ and its section equation. E is pseudonatural in T and in isomorphisms of target pairs.
hypotheses: X is a scheme or an algebraic stack on the fixed universe-bounded fppf site.
For a stack base, L and s mean compatible native sheaves and sections on all scheme test objects, as in SF.1/stack-quasi-coherent.
proofSteps: Use the existing equivalence [A¹/G_m](T)≃{native line,section}. The power functor is compared with the fixed native tensor-power recursion using the imported monoidal coherence.

Apply the objectwise categorical-pullback universal property, retaining the comparison isomorphism and its section-preservation equation. On arrows use exactly the root-arrow square, including the arrow of X.
Full faithfulness of the line-section equivalence and the 2-pullback give full faithfulness of E; lifting a line-section object and its identification gives essential surjectivity.

The root pullback coherence and the strong naturality of the imported comparison supply the identity/composition modifications. For a stack base evaluate on every T→X; QCoh pullback compatibility and native-effective-descent glue the comparisons.
acceptance: The projections to X agree up to the specified 2-isomorphism.
For X=BG_m and n=1 the comparison gives X itself, preserving the base automorphisms.

sources.match: The isomorphism in the root triple is exactly the datum retained in the 2-fibre-product presentation.
The stack, quotient, root and compatible sheaf carriers already have an upstream owner. This node compares them with the accepted native presentation rather than defining them again.

api.name: FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv
api.statement: E:R_n(X;L,s)≃rootStack n (L,s) is a strong equivalence over X, with root-preserving unit and counit.

api.name: FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_obj
api.statement: At T and x:T→X, E sends (M,t,φ) to (x,(M,t),φ) through the native line-section and tensor-power comparisons.

api.name: FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_hom
api.statement: The map on Hom sets is bijective and retains both the root section square and power-identification square, as well as the arrow of X.

api.name: FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_pullback
api.statement: For h:Y→T the strong naturality isomorphism has underlying native line-pullback comparison; its identity and composition modifications satisfy triangle and pentagon.

api.name: FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_targetIso
api.statement: An isomorphism (L,s)≅(L′,s′) postcomposes φ and commutes with E; identity and composition comparisons use those of the native tensor/pullback API.

api.name: FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_overStack
api.statement: For every scheme T→X, restriction of E is the scheme-base comparison for (L_T,s_T), with compatibility along all arrows of the test category of X.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_one
tests.statement: For n=1, E followed by upstream rootStack.one identifies (M,t,φ) with its base object; M,t are identified with L,s by φ.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_zero_stabilizer
tests.statement: At a geometric zero of s, E identifies the relative automorphism group of the zero-section root with the group scheme μ_n, even when the geometric field has characteristic dividing n.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_stack_base
tests.statement: For X=BG_m, L=O_X, s=1 and any n≥1, R_n≃X over X. The absolute automorphism group of the trivial base torsor is still G_m, whereas the relative automorphism group is trivial.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.nativeEquiv_nontrivial_pair
tests.statement: Over P¹_Q, the root (O(1),0,φ:O(1)^2≅O(2)) is carried to the 2-pullback object with that same line. Replacing all root lines by O fails.

uses.how: Transfers upstream stack geometry to the accepted native finite roots.
Retains 2-isomorphisms of the base and the native universal root.

nodes.title: Universal root and its classifying property
nodes.statement: Under E, the upstream universal line U_n, section τ_n and power identification α_n:U_n^n≅π*L pull back to the accepted universal native root. For any scheme T→X, giving a map T→R_n over X with its base 2-identification is equivalent, naturally in T, to giving a native root (M,t,φ) on T; arrows of maps correspond to root isomorphisms. Pullback of the universal triple gives this equivalence and identifies both φ(t^n)=s and the two equations on arrows. Universality is a groupoid equivalence, not a bijection on isomorphism classes.
hypotheses: Same X,L,s,n and universe bounds as native-upstream-equivalence.
proofSteps: Evaluate the second projection of the upstream 2-pullback and its structural 2-isomorphism. The line-section comparison gives U_n,τ_n,α_n.

Apply the 2-Yoneda equivalence to native-upstream-equivalence. Naturality yields the classifying map and its action on arrows; full faithfulness gives uniqueness up to unique compatible 2-isomorphism.
acceptance: Pullback along a classifying map recovers the whole input root triple, including φ.
For s=0 over a field, universal automorphisms retain their μ_n labels.

sources.match: The tautological root line in the quotient and 2-pullback presentations gives the universal triple; the native comparison identifies that triple.

nodes.title: Coherent arbitrary base change of the comparison
nodes.statement: For any 1-morphism g:Y→X of algebraic stacks, the accepted native base-change equivalence R_n(Y;g*L,g*s)≃Y×_X R_n(X;L,s), the upstream rootStack.baseChange equivalence, and E_Y,E_X form a 2-commutative square over Y. Its comparison is specified by the native line-pullback isomorphism and the structural 2-pullback isomorphism. It carries the universal triple to its pullback. Identity, composable base changes and 2-isomorphic base changes satisfy the unit, associativity and modification laws. No flatness is assumed.
hypotheses: Use 2-pullbacks throughout; g may be nonrepresentable or nonflat.
proofSteps: Use associativity of the imported 2-pullback, not a strict pullback of object sets. On each test scheme compare (M,t,φ) by the native pullback and tensor-power comparison.

Both paths have the same projections and structural isomorphism. The 2-universal property determines their comparison, and its full faithfulness proves coherence for identity, composition and 2-cells.
Use native-universal-root-comparison to identify the universal section and power isomorphism in this square.
acceptance: Z→F_p is allowed, including a change that sends a nonzero section to zero.
For X=BG_m the square compares groupoids over Y, without discarding the base 2-isomorphism.

sources.match: Both root constructions commute with pulling back the target pair.
The root-stack base-change comparison is canonical; this target adds its comparison with native pullback and coherent 2-cells.

nodes.title: Native affine roots and the torsor quotient
nodes.statement: Let X=Spec A, choose a frame l of L and write s=f·l. Put W=Spec A[z]/(z^n−f), with the weight-one μ_n action on z. Under E the native root stack is equivalent to the existing quotient [W/μ_n] over X, naturally in arbitrary ring maps and compatibly with changes of l. For a native root, the sheaf P of frames e of M satisfying φ(e^n)=l is a μ_n-torsor; the coordinate t=z e defines a map P→W. With right action e·ζ=ζe, its coordinate satisfies z(e·ζ)=ζ^−1 z(e); this is equivariance for the left weight-one action on W. Conversely a torsor and such a map descend O_P,t and φ. This is an equivalence of groupoids, including torsor isomorphisms, not just an orbit-set calculation.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring and n≥1.
The frame l is local data; changes of l use the native frame-change comparisons, not globally chosen n-th roots.
proofSteps: The normalized-frame sheaf is locally nonempty by RS.0/native-local-normalization; two frames differ by a unique μ_n section, proving the torsor identity. This uses fppf covers even in wild characteristic.
On P the root is trivialized; its section and power isomorphism satisfy the displayed equations. Effective descent constructs the inverse on objects and arrows.
Compare with the upstream affineChart via its tautological normalized root. The equality on frames and arrows determines the natural isomorphism by full faithfulness.
Use native-basechange-square and the RS.0 frame-change/coefficient comparisons for arbitrary ring maps and noncanonical frame changes; the cocycles are root isomorphisms.
acceptance: For f=0 and n>1, W→Spec A is not a μ_n-torsor in general; W→[W/μ_n] is the torsor used here.
For A=Z/4, n=2, the root with t=0 and φ coefficient 3 need not have an A-valued normalized frame; its torsor still gives an object of the quotient.
The formula z(e·ζ)=ζ^−1z(e) prevents reversing the associated-line convention.

sources.match: Normalize the power identification using an fppf μ_n-torsor to obtain the finite affine equation. The finite quotient comparison follows from that normalization and torsor descent, not from the false product-isomorphism assertion on p.54 (E13).
The finite logarithmic root chart is a finite diagonalizable torsor quotient; the rank-one case agrees with this affine root chart.

nodes.title: A smooth presentation valid for wild roots
nodes.statement: For the affine pair (A,f) put V_n(f)=Spec A[z,q,q^−1]/(z^n−q f). Give it the left G_m action λ·(z,q)=(λz,λ^nq). The map V_n(f)→R_n(Spec A;O,f) sends (z,q) to the trivial root line with section z and power identification of coefficient q^−1. It exhibits V_n(f) as the G_m-torsor of arbitrary frames of the universal root, hence is representable, smooth and surjective. There is an equivalence [V_n(f)/G_m]≃R_n and a comparison V_n(f)≃W×^{μ_n}G_m, where W has its weight-one action and μ_n acts on W×G_m by ζ·(w,λ)=(ζw,λζ^−1); the latter comparison sends (w,λ) to (λw,λ^n).
hypotheses: Any commutative A, f∈A and positive n; no invertibility of n.
V_n(f) is a presentation over Spec A, not a claim that V_n(f)→Spec A is smooth.
proofSteps: A frame e of the root line gives t=z e and φ(e^n)=q^−1, so the root equation is z^n=qf. Conversely these coordinates construct a root with its frame.

Forgetting an arbitrary frame is a G_m-torsor on each test scheme by native line local triviality; G_m is smooth, so this is a smooth atlas. Its action on the trivial root is the arrow of unit label λ.

The generic torsor quotient equivalence identifies [V/G_m] with the root stack. Normalizing q by a μ_n cover gives the contracted-product comparison; descend the invariant map (w,λ)↦(λw,λ^n). For representability view the power map G_m→G_m, λ↦q=λ^n, as the μ_n-torsor over the q-base and form its associated W-bundle; W itself is not asserted to be a torsor.
acceptance: The atlas is smooth as a map to the stack in characteristic p with n=p.

sources.match: The frame presentation uses a smooth G_m atlas even when the finite root group is not smooth. Our q is the inverse of the coefficient of the power identification. The product-isomorphism assertion at the top of p.54 is false in this preprint (source issue E13); the contracted-product comparison here is instead derived from the explicit invariant coordinate map and torsor descent.
Representability of torsors, contracted products and smooth quotient atlases are imported general results.

api.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation
api.statement: The chosen affine frame l identifies the universal-root frame torsor with V_n(f), by the coordinate equations z^n=qf and φ coefficient q^−1.

api.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation_action
api.statement: Changing a frame by e↦λ^−1 e sends (z,q) to (λz,λ^nq); the induced root arrow has label λ.

api.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation_torsor
api.statement: V→R is a representable G_m-torsor; V×_R V≃G_m×V with the source, target and composition of this action.

api.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation_quotient
api.statement: The quotient [V/G_m]→R is an equivalence over Spec A, sending the tautological root to the native universal root.

api.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation_finiteChart
api.statement: The map W×G_m→V, (w,λ)↦(λw,λ^n), induces V≃W×^{μ_n}G_m with the stated inverse action on λ.

api.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation_baseChange
api.statement: Every A→B identifies the base change of V_n(f) and its atlas/action with V_n(f_B), with identity and composition comparisons induced on both coordinates.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation_one
tests.statement: For n=1, eliminate z=qf: V_1(f)≅Spec A[q,q^−1]; its map to the root stack is the ordinary frame G_m-torsor over Spec A.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation_zero
tests.statement: For f=0, V_n(0)=Spec A[z,q,q^−1]/(z^n). For a field and n>1 this atlas is nonreduced, although its map to the root stack is smooth.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation_wild
tests.statement: For A=F_p[x], f=x and n=p, the atlas is Spec F_p[z,q,q^−1], via x=q^−1z^p, and is regular. The finite chart W→R is a μ_p-torsor and is not smooth.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation_unit
tests.statement: For f a unit, eliminate q=z^n/f to obtain V_n(f)≅Spec A[z,z^−1]; the G_m action scales z and its quotient is Spec A.

tests.name: FiniteRoot.smoothPresentation_not_product
tests.statement: For A=C, f=1 and n=2, V_2(1) is G_m and is connected, while W_2(1) is two reduced points and W_2(1)×G_m has two connected components. The comparison must take the antidiagonal μ_2 quotient; the product itself is not isomorphic to V_2(1).

uses.how: Provides the actual smooth scheme atlas needed for regularity without treating μ_p as smooth.
Identifies the geometric presentation with the native universal-root frame torsor.

nodes.title: Algebraicity and finite relative diagonal
nodes.statement: The native root stack of any pair on an algebraic stack X is algebraic. Its projection π:R_n→X is flat and locally of finite presentation, with finite relative diagonal. For scheme X its absolute inertia is finite. For a general stack base, these are relative assertions; no finiteness or triviality of the absolute stabilizers of X is assumed. On an affine frame chart W→R is a finite locally free μ_n-torsor of rank n; W→X is finite locally free of rank n, whereas W→X is generally not a torsor.
hypotheses: X is algebraic, L invertible, s arbitrary, n≥1.
Finite diagonal means representable and finite, without asserting flatness of the Isom spaces after imposing the section equation.
proofSteps: For a scheme base use native-smooth-presentation and the upstream quotient algebraicity theorem, or transport the existing rootStack geometry along E. For a stack base use its smooth scheme atlas and native-basechange-square.
The finite chart W→R is a μ_n-torsor and W→X is defined by a monic degree-n equation. Flatness and local finite presentation of π follow fppf locally from these two maps.

For two roots over the same T, isomorphisms of their n-th-power data form a μ_n-torsor locally. The extra equation a(t)=t′ cuts out a closed subscheme. Thus the relative Isom space is finite, but need not be flat. For X a scheme this gives finite inertia.
acceptance: At a wild branch point over F_p the stack is algebraic with finite nonreduced relative inertia.
For X=BG_m and n=1, π is the identity, so the absolute inertia is G_m rather than finite.

sources.match: The finite root chart and smooth frame presentation give the root-specific algebraicity and local finite flat covers.
Algebraicity, relative properties and inertia are owned by the supplier; this is their transport to native roots.

nodes.title: The relative coarse space of native roots
nodes.statement: For a scheme X, the native projection π:R_n(X;L,s)→X is a coarse moduli morphism: it is categorical for maps to every algebraic space, and induces a bijection on geometric isomorphism classes over every algebraically closed field. Its formation commutes with arbitrary base change, including nonflat base change, and its quasi-coherent pushforward is exact. For an algebraic-stack base X these statements hold after every scheme T→X and coherently on their overlaps. In particular π has the corresponding relative universal property for algebraic spaces over X (representable targets over X), interpreted with compatible 2-isomorphisms. It does not assert that X is an absolute algebraic space or an absolute coarse space.
hypotheses: Any n≥1 and arbitrary section; a Cartier or regularity hypothesis is unnecessary.
The generic finite-diagonalizable coarse quotient theorem in request RS1-DIAGONALIZABLE-COARSE is a required supplier input. A constant finite-group theorem is insufficient when n is not invertible.
proofSteps: On an affine trivialization use native-quotient-comparison. The accepted parent affine-invariant-algebra-equivalence identifies the Hopf-coaction equalizer in A[z]/(z^n−f) with A; this calculation uses all characters, not μ_n(A)-points.

Apply the requested finite-diagonalizable quotient coarse universal property, including maps to nonaffine algebraic spaces, to conclude that the candidate Spec A is coarse. The degree-zero projection on graded equivariant modules makes invariants exact and compatible with arbitrary tensor base change, including wild μ_p. This is the supplier input, not an inference from the invariant ring alone.

Glue the coarse identifications on affine overlaps by the uniqueness of the coarse universal property. Their agreement with arbitrary base change follows either from the supplier theorem or from its tame-base-change corollary after the chartwise exactness.

nodes.title: Full geometric fibres and the zero-section gerbe
nodes.statement: For a geometric point x:Spec K→X (K algebraically closed), the 2-fibre of the native projection is [Spec K[z]/(z^n−f_x)/μ_n] after choosing a frame of L_x. If s_x≠0 it is equivalent to Spec K. If s_x=0 it contains the zero-root-section gerbe G_x of n-th roots of L_x as a closed substack cut out by the universal root section; its ideal is nilpotent with n-th power zero. After choosing a frame of L_x this gerbe is B_K μ_n and is the reduction of the full fibre. For n>1 the full fibre is nonreduced and differs from G_x. This remains true when char K divides n; Bμ_n itself is reduced as an algebraic stack, despite μ_n possibly being nonreduced.
hypotheses: The assertion concerns the relative 2-fibre along the specified geometric point even when X is a stack.
Neutralization G_x≃Bμ_n depends on a frame of L_x; the gerbe itself is intrinsic.
proofSteps: Use native-basechange-square and native-quotient-comparison for the full fibre. If f_x is a unit, z is a unit on the chart and the μ_n action is free with quotient Spec K.
When f_x=0, the equivariant ideal (z) is nilpotent of exponent n; its quotient stack is the zero-section root gerbe. A frame of L_x identifies this gerbe with Bμ_n.

The smooth G_m atlas of Bμ_n is G_m via the power action, so that gerbe is reduced even for μ_p. The full fibre has smooth atlas Spec K[z,q,q^−1]/z^n from native-smooth-presentation. For n>1 its z is nonzero nilpotent, proving the distinction without using K-valued points alone.
acceptance: Over K[ε]/ε² with n=2, the trivial root with section ε is an object over the zero target section but is not isomorphic to the zero-section root.
For n=1 and f_x=0 the fibre and its gerbe are both Spec K.
For char K=p,n=p, the dual-number unit 1+ε is a nonidentity automorphism of the zero root, although μ_p(K) has one point.

sources.locator: Appendix B.2, p.53, nilpotent closed embedding and infinitesimal-neighbourhood description

The owned root stack explicitly distinguishes the full infinitesimal fibre from its reduced gerbe; this target transports that distinction to native data.

nodes.title: Regular roots of regular Cartier divisors
nodes.statement: Let X be a regular scheme and D a regular effective Cartier divisor. For every positive integer n, the native root stack R_n(X;O(D),s_D) is a regular algebraic stack, where regularity is checked on a smooth surjective scheme atlas. No invertibility of n is required. On an affine trivialization with equation f, the actual smooth-presentation ring A[z,q,q^−1]/(z^n−qf) is regular whenever A is a regular ring, f is a nonzerodivisor and A/(f) is regular.
hypotheses: Regular schemes are locally Noetherian with regular local rings. D is effective Cartier and itself regular; an arbitrary Cartier divisor is insufficient.
Regularity of X is absolute; regularity after arbitrary base change is not asserted.
proofSteps: Cover X by affine opens framing O(D). The chosen smooth atlas is native-smooth-presentation; using the finite μ_n atlas as if it were smooth would be invalid in wild characteristic.

For n=1 eliminate z=qf. For n≥2 work in the regular ambient A[z,q,q^−1]. At a prime containing z, also f lies in the prime; since A/(f) is regular and f is a nonzerodivisor, f is a local regular parameter. Equivalently, quotienting the ambient regular local ring by f is regular, so its class in the cotangent space is nonzero.

The class of z^n−qf in the ambient cotangent space equals −qf and is nonzero. Extend it to a regular system of parameters; quotient by this parameter is regular. This uses Stacks Lemmas 10.106.3–10.106.4.

On z≠0, f is invertible and the equation eliminates q: the ring is A_f[z,z^−1], which is regular. Glue these local regularity statements and apply the smooth-local property/atlas independence of regularity.
acceptance: For X=A¹_F_p,D=(x),n=p, the smooth atlas is Spec F_p[z,q,q^−1] and is regular although the root stack is not DM over D.
For a unit f, the atlas is A[z,z^−1] and the stack is X, in every characteristic.
For X=A¹_k,D=(x²),n=2,char k≠2, D is Cartier but not regular and the root chart at x=z=0 is nodal. Thus the hypothesis that D is regular cannot be dropped.

sources.match: Supplies the smooth frame atlas. The regularity argument here is a deduction from that atlas, not a regularity theorem attributed to AGV.

sources.locator: Lemmas 10.106.3–10.106.4 (00NN); Lemma 10.163.10 (07NF); §100.7, Lemma 100.7.1, Definition 100.7.2 and Remark 100.7.3 (04YE/04YG); tag pages, no fixed pagination
sources.match: Quotients by a regular parameter stay regular, smooth algebras over regular bases are regular, and regularity of algebraic stacks is a smooth-local property.

nodes.title: The exact Deligne–Mumford locus
nodes.statement: For a scheme X and any pair (L,s), write D=V(s) for its scheme-theoretic zero locus, without assuming Cartier or regularity. The native root stack is Deligne–Mumford if and only if n is a unit on D. Its DM locus is exactly the inverse image of (X∖|D|)∪D(n), where D(n) is the open subset on which the integer n is invertible. At a geometric branch point its relative inertia is μ_n; away from D it is trivial. For an algebraic-stack base this is a criterion for π:R_n→X to be a DM morphism; the whole root stack is DM if X is DM and this condition holds. No assertion about the absolute DM locus of an arbitrary non-DM base is made.
hypotheses: Positive n; arbitrary section. Empty D gives the whole base even if n is not a unit on X.
At general nonreduced test objects, the relative automorphism sheaf of a root is the subgroup of G_m given by λ^n=1 and (λ−1)t=0, not identically μ_n.
proofSteps: Under native-quotient-comparison, compute geometric stabilizers: a nonzero section forces λ=1, and a zero section leaves precisely μ_n. Use the supplier inertia and quotient DM criterion.

The group scheme μ_n over a field is unramified exactly when n is nonzero in that field. At wild branch points the tangent unit 1+ε gives a nonzero tangent vector, proving failure of unramifiedness even though the geometric point group may have one element.

Unramifiedness of the relative diagonal is a local property. Its locus therefore consists precisely of the preimage of the displayed base open. Testing every point of D is equivalent to n being invertible on D.
For a stack base make the same calculation after every scheme test map using native-basechange-square; combine a DM morphism with a DM base for the stated absolute conclusion.
acceptance: For X=Spec Z, s=p,n=p (p prime), the root stack is DM off p and is not DM above p.
For X=Spec Z,s=1,n=p, the root stack is X and is DM everywhere.
For X=Spec Z,s=2,n=3, n is not a unit on X but is a unit on V(2); the root stack is DM everywhere.
For char K=p,n=p, (1+ε)^p=1 in K[ε]/ε² detects nonreduced inertia; pointwise roots of unity do not detect the failure.
